Smart Reads of the Week: DBS Dividend Income, Temasek Stocks, SGX Share Buybacks, and REIT Recovery
article:
Singapore’s STI fell 1.4% to around 5,011 in Friday morning trading, tracking a sharp sell-off on Wall Street as local bank shares came under pressure.
Over in the US, the S&P 500 fell 2% on Thursday, marking its sixth consecutive decline, while the Nasdaq dropped 2.3% amid continued concerns over AI stocks.
With markets under pressure, investors have good reason to focus on dividend income, business fundamentals and long-term opportunities.
This week’s Smart Reads explores how much dividend income S$10,000 invested in DBS could generate in 2027, alongside Temasek-backed companies paying extra dividends and blue chips rewarding shareholders through share buybacks.
We also examine record fee income at UOB and iFAST, uncover four overlooked SGX companies delivering strong revenue growth, and consider whether Singapore REITs are finally making a comeback.
Finally, we take a closer look at Nvidia’s 35% decline and what long-term investors should consider before buying, holding or selling.
Here are this week’s top articles:
S$10,000 in DBS Shares: How Much Dividend Income Could You Receive in 2027?
Find out how much passive income a S$10,000 investment in DBS could generate next year.
5 Temasek-Backed SGX Stocks Rewarding Shareholders with Extra Dividends
These five Temasek-backed companies are rewarding investors with additional payouts. We examine what is driving them.
Get Smart: Nvidia Has Fallen 35%. Should You Buy, Hold or Sell?
Nvidia’s sharp decline raises questions about its valuation, growth prospects and what investors should do next.
Record Fees at UOB and iFAST: Where Singapore’s Wealth Is Flowing
Rising fee income at UOB and iFAST reveals how Singapore’s wealth management industry is evolving.
Revenue Growth of 20% or More: 4 Overlooked SGX Stocks
These four lesser-known Singapore companies are delivering impressive revenue growth. Can they sustain their momentum?
Top 3 Blue-Chip Dividend Stocks Aggressively Buying Back Shares
Three established blue chips are buying back shares. We explore what these moves could mean for shareholders.
SGX Next 50: 3 Dividend Stocks Quietly Buying Back Shares
Beyond the STI, these three dividend-paying companies are using share buybacks to return value to investors.
Is the Great Singapore REIT Comeback Finally Here?
After a challenging period, Singapore REITs are attracting attention again. We examine whether a recovery is taking shape.
